name: Future Circular Collider (electron-positron stage, FCC-ee)
notes: The Atlas marker is the CERN Meyrin campus, the host laboratory; the proposed ring lies underground beneath CERN and the surrounding regions of France and Switzerland (CERN FCC page).
Status is "proposed": the CERN Council decision on whether to build is planned for 2028 (CERN, 22 May 2026: "the Council will be in a position, by 2028, to take a decision on the FCC-ee").
The FCC programme page also describes a possible later proton-proton stage (FCC-hh); only the electron-positron stage is recorded here.

circumference.quote: 90.7 kilometres The circumference of the accelerator ring

depth.note: Average depth of the tunnel; the page also gives a range of 180 to 400 m.
depth.quote: The FCC would be housed in a 91-kilometre tunnel at an average depth of 200 metres underneath CERN and the surrounding regions of France and Switzerland, including a section passing beneath Lake Geneva.

summary.plain: A proposed 91-kilometre electron-positron collider in a new tunnel beneath the CERN area and neighbouring France and Switzerland, intended as a Higgs factory. The feasibility study was published in March 2025 and the 2026 European Strategy update recommends it; the CERN Council is to decide by 2028. It is not approved.
summary.technical: FCC-ee: proposed 90.7 km circumference e+e- collider in an underground tunnel at 180-400 m depth (200 m average) beneath Haute-Savoie, Ain and the canton of Geneva, the first stage of the FCC programme, which might later be converted to a proton-proton collider. Feasibility Study Report (three volumes, March 2025). European Strategy 2026 update (22 May 2026) recommends FCC-ee as the preferred next flagship at CERN; a Council decision is planned by 2028; if approved: civil engineering 2033-2040, installation after 2038, operation after 2045.
